title: Technical Analysis Hub
html:
the desk’s primary lens is technical analysis, with Fibonacci as the main tool. Fundamentals and the Fed are context; the chart is the trigger.

Notes

  • Fibonacci Playbook — how we draw and trade Fib levels
  • Indicators Cheat Sheet — moving averages, RSI, ATR, volume
  • Technical Funds & Traders — who makes money from price action, and what to borrow
  • Edge Study 2026-10-17 — backtest of our setups (upside edge modest, no downside edge yet)
  • X Accounts — who we follow on X
  • Watchlist — current levels on SPY, XOM, TSLA, AAPL
  • Options Playbook — turning a chart setup into a call/put trade

The house method (draft — will evolve)

  1. Trend first: price vs. 50- and 200-day averages. Trade with the trend unless there's a clear reversal.
  2. Map the swing: draw Fibonacci from the last major swing low to high (or high to low).
  3. Look for confluence: a Fib level that lines up with a moving average, a prior high/low, or a round number is stronger than a Fib level alone.
  4. Confirm: wait for price to react at the level (reversal candle, RSI turning, volume).
  5. Define the trade before entering: entry, stop (the next Fib level beyond), and target (the next Fib level or extension).
  6. Check the calendar: earnings and Fed days can blow through any level.

Data source

Levels in this vault are calculated from Webull daily bars (dividend-adjusted, so older prices can sit slightly below what was quoted at the time).
